name: clickables

operatingThreshold.rule: the threshold with the best F1 on the calibration websites; the test websites are never used to choose it

selection.reason: The graph network missed the ship gate. The gradient-boosting fallback ships only if it passes precision and calibration, and it did not, so the graph network ships, switched off by default.

architecture: SIGN-style network: 6 view encoders (92->48), head 288->48->1; 40705 parameters

data.note: Tranco top-1,000 crawl. Every row from pages with document-level (delegated) click listeners was removed, whatever its label.

comparisons.model: Rule: pointer cursor and not native

seeds.rule: the seed with the highest PR-AUC on the calibration websites; test scores are never used
seeds.note: test PR-AUC of the graph network trained with each seed, in seed order

latency.target: <= 50 ms for 2,000 elements in the Web Worker
latency.note: median of 10 runs in the app's Web Worker; headless Chromium, 12 × 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1255U, no CPU throttling

summary: The model is experimental and switched off by default. Its suggestions are advisory and never change the score, the history or the report.

Earlier results were inflated by label leakage. The earlier training filter dropped rows from pages with delegated (document-level) click listeners only when their label was 0, and kept every positive. Counting the raw crawl by page type and label showed that it kept 8,691 positives from delegated pages and only 60 from other pages, while every negative it kept came from a non-delegated page, so the page type gave the label away. The filter now drops whole delegated pages, whatever their labels, and every number on this card comes from that corrected run.

There are only 60 trustworthy positives, from 13 websites. The test split has 6 of them, from 2 websites, so the 95% intervals below cover nearly the whole range from 0 to 1. This run cannot measure how good the model is.

No threshold reached 90% precision on the calibration websites, so the precision gate is not met ("not reached"). Separately from the ship gate, the app makes suggestions at an operating threshold chosen by one fixed rule: the threshold with the best F1 on the calibration websites (the test websites are never used to choose it). That threshold is 0.00064, because the model ranks the calibration positives no better than chance, so the best F1 comes from flagging almost everything. On the test websites it flags 2,074 of 2,608 elements: precision 0.3% (95% interval 0.0% to 0.5%) and recall 100% (6 of 6; 95% interval 100% to 100%). Every suggestion is labelled low confidence.
failurePatterns: The errors have not been reviewed by hand. errors.json holds samples taken at the operating threshold: 50 of the 2,068 false positives on the test websites; there are no false negatives. No recurring causes are claimed.
limitations: The shipped model is the SIGN graph network trained with seed 2, the weakest of the three seeds on the test websites (PR-AUC 0.176, against 0.504 for seed 0 and 0.503 for seed 1). The pipeline picks the seed with the highest PR-AUC on the calibration websites, and seed 2 scored highest there, but all three scored about 0.004, below the 0.005 share of click-only controls on those websites, so the choice was close to arbitrary. Seeds are never switched by test score.

The Tranco top-1,000 crawl produced 1,407 page records; 879 pages were used. After every row from delegated pages was removed, 9,654 candidate rows from 136 websites remain, and only 13 of those websites have any click-only control. One website (capcut.com) has 32 of the 60.
All examples come from the Tranco crawl. The corpus has no Vue or Angular pages, and the results are not representative of other kinds of websites.

labelProbe.method: Random sample of labelled candidates; each clicked once at its centre in the live page. "responds": the DOM, address or a dialog changed within 400 ms. Skipped as untestable: pages that change by themselves, and elements whose centre is a link or button. A response can still come from a handler on an ancestor, so disagreement is an upper bound on label noise.

labelHandCheck.method: Method (ml/README.md, step 2): labels/sheet.mjs drew 300 random labelled elements; labels/audit.mjs re-checked each one in the live page with Chrome's DevTools Protocol, reading the element's own listeners and React handlers, its ancestors' and any document-level (delegated) listeners, and marked it correct, wrong or unsure; labels/score.mjs counted the verdicts. The check is automated: an independent manual review by the owner has not been done.
labelHandCheck.reading: This measures whether the labels are accurate, and that still holds after the filter change, because filtering removes rows but does not change any label. It does not fix the small number of positives: only 4 of the judged labels were positive, and the corrected corpus has only 60.
